sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Rachel Abrams, and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的雷切尔·艾布拉姆斯，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Since the war with Iran began, President Trump has gone from urging Iranians to take cover and protect themselves to threatening to annihilate them.
sentences.zh: 自从与伊朗的战争爆发以来，特朗普总统的态度从敦促伊朗人寻找掩护、保护自己，变成了威胁要彻底消灭他们。

sentences.en: But with the ceasefire set to expire this week, very little has been heard from the Iranian people themselves.
sentences.zh: 但随着停火协议将于本周到期，人们几乎听不到伊朗人民自己的声音。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Claire Tennesketter speaks to Iranians about how they view this war.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事克莱尔·特内斯凯特采访了伊朗人，了解他们如何看待这场战争。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, April 21St.
sentences.zh: 今天是4月21日，星期二。

sentences.en: To the great, proud people of Iran, I say tonight that the hour of your freedom is at hand.
sentences.zh: 我对伟大而自豪的伊朗人民说，今晚，你们获得自由的时刻已经来临。

sentences.en: The day the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: and Israel launched its joint military operation against Iran,
sentences.zh: 和以色列对伊朗发动联合军事行动的那天，

sentences.en: President Trump posted a video on True Social.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统在“真实社交”上发布了一段视频。

sentences.en: When we are finished, take over your government.
sentences.zh: 当我们结束后，接管你们的政府。

sentences.en: It will be yours to take.
sentences.zh: 这个政权将由你们来接管。

sentences.en: This will be probably your only chance for generations.
sentences.zh: 这可能是你们几代人中唯一的机遇。

sentences.en: He urged the Iranian people to rise up against the government.
sentences.zh: 他敦促伊朗人民奋起反抗政府。

sentences.en: Now is the time to seize control of your destiny and to unleash the prosperous and glorious future that is close within your reach.
sentences.zh: 现在是掌握你们命运、释放触手可及的繁荣与辉煌未来的时刻。

sentences.en: This is the moment for action.
sentences.zh: 现在正是采取行动的时刻。

sentences.en: Do not let it pass.
sentences.zh: 不要让它错失。

sentences.en: But then bombs started to fall.
sentences.zh: 但随后炸弹开始落下。

sentences.en: People did not rise up.
sentences.zh: 人们并没有奋起反抗。

sentences.en: And so I wondered, what did Iranians think of this new war and the president's call to action?
sentences.zh: 因此我禁不住想，伊朗人如何看待这场新战争以及总统的行动号召？

sentences.en: So I started reaching out to them.
sentences.zh: 于是我开始联系他们。

sentences.en: In the first days of the war, I sent nearly 100 messages, mostly to residents of Tehran, the site of some of the heaviest bombing.
sentences.zh: 在战争初期，我发了近100条消息，大多发给德黑兰的居民，那里曾遭到一些最猛烈的轰炸。

sentences.en: Still, I heard nothing.
sentences.zh: 然而，我没有听到任何回复。

sentences.en: I could see most of my messages weren't even being opened.
sentences.zh: 我能看到我的大部分消息甚至都没有被打开。

sentences.en: It wasn't that people didn't want to talk.
sentences.zh: 并不是人们不想说话。

sentences.en: They couldn't.
sentences.zh: 而是他们做不到。

sentences.en: Not only is it extremely dangerous for Iranians to speak to an American journalist, phone calls could be monitored by the regime.
sentences.zh: 伊朗人与美国记者交谈不仅极其危险，而且通话还可能遭到政权的监控。

sentences.en: Iran has been in the dark for days, forced into a near-total internet blackout.
sentences.zh: 伊朗已经黑暗了数日，被迫陷入近乎完全的互联网黑洞。

sentences.en: But the bigger problem was a communication blackout.
sentences.zh: 但更大的问题是通信中断。

sentences.en: Days have passed without word from family and friends.
sentences.zh: 好几天都听不到家人和朋友的消息。

sentences.en: The Iranian government had effectively cut off the country from the rest of the world.
sentences.zh: 伊朗政府实际上切断了该国与世界其他地区的联系。

sentences.en: The number I kept seeing was 99%.
sentences.zh: 我不断看到的数字是99%。

sentences.en: 99% of Iranians who normally had access to the internet now didn't.
sentences.zh: 99%原本能够上网的伊朗人现在上不了网了。

sentences.en: I was trying to reach the remaining 1%.
sentences.zh: 我试图联系剩下的1%。

sentences.en: These would be people with workarounds, like VPNs, or enough money to afford satellite communications like Starlink, that could get them online for even just a few minutes.
sentences.zh: 这些人会使用变通方法，比如VPN，或者有足够的钱购买星链等卫星通信设备，哪怕只能让他们在线短短几分钟。

sentences.en: And then, almost a week into the war, my colleagues and I got a few replies.
sentences.zh: 然后，在战争进行了将近一周时，我和同事收到了一些回复。

sentences.en: Hello?
sentences.zh: 喂？

sentences.en: Some of them only had enough internet to send text messages.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人只有足够的互联网流量来发送短信。

sentences.en: But others were able to send short voice memos.
sentences.zh: 但其他人则能够发送简短的语音备忘录。

sentences.en: I am in my own bedroom.
sentences.zh: 我正待在自己的卧室里。

sentences.en: I can say we've been through a lot lately.
sentences.zh: 可以说我们最近经历了很多。

sentences.en: One, two, one, one!
sentences.zh: 一，二，一，一！

sentences.en: We heard a loud explosion.
sentences.zh: 我们听到了一声巨响。

sentences.en: I heard some loud bomb noises.
sentences.zh: 我听到了一些巨大的轰炸声。

sentences.en: At that time, people were still reeling from the war's initial shocks.
sentences.zh: 当时，人们仍未从战争初期的冲击中缓过神来。

sentences.en: I woke up.
sentences.zh: 我醒了过来。

sentences.en: And shortly after that, a huge cloud of smoke drifted into our classroom.
sentences.zh: 紧接着，一大团烟雾飘进了我们的教室。

sentences.en: Right now, the Iranian state media is telling the people of Iran that the Ayatollah has been killed.
sentences.zh: 目前，伊朗国家媒体正在告诉伊朗人民，阿亚图拉已经被杀。

sentences.en: Iran's Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, had just been killed in an airstrike.
sentences.zh: 伊朗最高领袖阿亚图拉阿里·哈梅内伊刚刚在一次空袭中身亡。

sentences.en: Many of the people I spoke with were critical of the regime, like the vast majority of Iranians.
sentences.zh: 我和许多交过谈的人都对政权持批评态度，就像绝大多数伊朗人一样。

sentences.en: Their spirits seemed high.
sentences.zh: 他们的情绪似乎很高涨。

sentences.en: People in the streets.
sentences.zh: 街上的人们。

sentences.en: We were chanting slogans and making the victory signs, saying military help from Israel and the United States.
sentences.zh: 我们高喊口号，做出胜利的手势，说来自以色列和美国的军事援助。

sentences.en: It's here.
sentences.zh: 它来了。

sentences.en: It finally happened.
sentences.zh: 它终于发生了。

sentences.en: They are here.
sentences.zh: 他们来了。

sentences.en: Then, there were the Iranians who supported the regime.
sentences.zh: 然后，还有支持政权的伊朗人。

sentences.en: Many of those people were grieving.
sentences.zh: 其中许多人在悲伤。

sentences.en: But others were angry and pledged to fight against the American and Israeli invaders.
sentences.zh: 但另一些人则很愤怒，并誓言要与美国和以色列侵略者战斗到底。

sentences.en: One Iranian who supported the regime said he heard people chanting, death to Trump.
sentences.zh: 一个支持政权的伊朗人说，他听到人们高喊“打倒特朗普”。

sentences.en: Every day, the bombs are being dropped.
sentences.zh: 炸弹每天都在投下。

sentences.en: When it came to Trump's call to overthrow the government, many of those opposed to the regime said it didn't make sense to take to the streets in proteSt.
sentences.zh: 谈到特朗普推翻政府的呼吁时，许多反对政权的人表示，上街抗议是没有意义的。

sentences.en: It was too dangerous.
sentences.zh: 这太危险了。

sentences.en: One source told me her friend's daughter was shot and killed on the street by what she described as pro-regime forces.
sentences.zh: 一位消息人士告诉我，她朋友的女儿在街上被她形容为亲政权部队的人开枪打死。

sentences.en: Because our neighbor who was a civilian was killed in an attack.
sentences.zh: 因为我们的邻居是一名平民，在一次袭击中丧生。

sentences.en: Another told me her neighbor was at work when he was killed by an airstrike.
sentences.zh: 另一个人告诉我，她的邻居在上班时死于空袭。

sentences.en: We weren't able to verify these stories.
sentences.zh: 我们无法核实这些故事。

sentences.en: Still, there were other, more complicated reasons people hadn't done the thing President Trump had imagined.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，人们没有做特朗普总统想象中那种事，还有其他更复杂的原因。

sentences.en: Reasons that were decades old and rooted in the very idea of resistance in Iran.
sentences.zh: 这些原因历经数十年，根植于伊朗的反抗理念本身。

sentences.en: I found two people who told me that much deeper story.
sentences.zh: 我找到了两个人，他们向我讲述了更深层次的故事。

sentences.en: Two people who have very different views on the war and the best way to change Iran.
sentences.zh: 这两个人对战争以及改变伊朗的最佳方式有着截然不同的看法。

sentences.en: However you are comfortable, can you introduce yourself to me?
sentences.zh: 以你觉得最舒服的方式，你能向我做个自我介绍吗？

sentences.en: What should I say?
sentences.zh: 我该说些什么？

sentences.en: I'm now leaving Europe, but I'm leaving here by force.
sentences.zh: 我现在正离开欧洲，但我是在被迫离开这里。

sentences.en: I reached a source who I'm going to refer to by his first initial, C.
sentences.zh: 我联系到了一位消息人士，我将用他的名字首字母C来称呼他。

sentences.en: He was at his aunt's apartment in Europe.
sentences.zh: 他当时在欧洲他阿姨的公寓里。

sentences.en: He had left Iran just days before the war broke out.
sentences.zh: 他在战争爆发前几天刚刚离开伊朗。

sentences.en: He initially tried to go back.
sentences.zh: 他最初试图回去。

sentences.en: His wife, his family, they were all in Tehran.
sentences.zh: 他的妻子、他的家人，他们全都在德黑兰。

sentences.en: But at that time, with airstrikes ongoing, there were no flights back home.
sentences.zh: 但当时空袭持续不断，已经没有回家的航班了。

sentences.en: So you're stuck and waiting to see what happens next?
sentences.zh: 所以你被困住了，在等着看接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 对，当然。

sentences.en: Yeah, right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It was a strange position to be in.
sentences.zh: 这是一种奇怪的处境。

sentences.en: Locked outside your country while it was under attack.
sentences.zh: 当你的国家遭受攻击时，你却被锁在国门之外。

sentences.en: But because he was in Europe, he felt freer to open up to me about his life in Iran.
sentences.zh: 但由于身在欧洲，他觉得更无拘无束，可以向我敞开心扉谈论他在伊朗的生活。

sentences.en: Can you tell me a little bit about your childhood, what it meant to you as a kid to be Iranian?
sentences.zh: 你能跟我讲讲你的童年吗，作为一个孩子，身为伊朗人对你意味着什么？

sentences.en: I was a quiet person.
sentences.zh: 我是一个安静的人。

sentences.en: Both of my parents worked outside.
sentences.zh: 我的父母都在外面工作。

sentences.en: C was born in the late 80s, around the time when the Islamic Republic was just a decade old.
sentences.zh: C出生于80年代末，大约是在伊斯兰共和国刚满十岁的时候。

sentences.en: He grew up in the outskirts of Tehran.
sentences.zh: 他在德黑兰郊区长大。

sentences.en: His mom worked an office job, and his dad was a mechanic.
sentences.zh: 他的妈妈做文职工作，爸爸是个机械师。

sentences.en: They would both work long hours.
sentences.zh: 他们俩都要工作很长时间。

sentences.en: We were alone for a long time during our childhood.
sentences.zh: 在我们的童年里，我们有很长一段时间都是孤身一人。

sentences.en: So C and his sister spent a lot of time with their grandfather.
sentences.zh: 所以C和他的姐姐花了很多时间和他们的祖父在一起。

sentences.en: And most of the time, we went to mosque.
sentences.zh: 而且大多数时候，我们都去清真寺。

sentences.en: And they're chanting,
sentences.zh: 他们在高喊着，

sentences.en: Death to America, Death to Israel.
sentences.zh: 打倒美国，打倒以色列。

sentences.en: It was in the mosque that he heard people chant,
sentences.zh: 正是在清真寺里，他听到人们高喊着，

sentences.en: Death to America.
sentences.zh: 打倒美国。

sentences.en: He said it was a sentiment that he heard in many places.
sentences.zh: 他说这是一种他在很多地方都能听到的情绪。

sentences.en: In school, on TV.
sentences.zh: 在学校里，在电视上。

sentences.en: But it wasn't until he got a little bit older that he really started to fixate on those words.
sentences.zh: 但直到他稍微长大一点，他才真正开始纠结于这些词语。

sentences.en: And I wondered why they're chanting these slogans.
sentences.zh: 我想知道为什么他们要喊这些口号。

sentences.en: Why we are doing this.
sentences.zh: 为什么我们要这样做。

sentences.en: God can't be like this.
sentences.zh: 上帝不可能是这样的。

sentences.en: That was the starting point to questioning the whole system.
sentences.zh: 那是质疑整个体制的起点。

sentences.en: So he wondered why Iran hated the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他想知道为什么伊朗讨厌西方。

sentences.en: Why some people, including his government, claimed that believing in Islam and being a good Muslim meant being against non-Muslim people.
sentences.zh: 为什么有些人，包括他的政府，声称信仰伊斯兰教并做一个好穆斯林就意味着反对非穆斯林。

sentences.en: But to even have these questions was scary to see.
sentences.zh: 但仅仅产生这些疑问就让人感到害怕。

sentences.en: I was scared a lot.
sentences.zh: 我感到非常害怕。

sentences.en: He'd heard stories of people being hanged for not believing in the government's messages.
sentences.zh: 他听说过有人因为不相信政府的信息而被绞死的故事。

sentences.en: They made us believe all the bad things will happen to you.
sentences.zh: 他们让我们相信所有坏事都会降临到你头上。

sentences.en: So he tried to not have them at all.
sentences.zh: 所以他尽量让自己根本不要去想这些。

sentences.en: He already felt like an outsider.
sentences.zh: 他本来就觉得自己像个局外人。

sentences.en: He was picked on and bullied at school.
sentences.zh: 他在学校里受人挑衅和欺负。

sentences.en: So to quietly wonder why things were the way they were made him feel even lonelier.
sentences.zh: 因此，默默地纳闷事情为什么会是这个样子，让他感到更加孤独。

sentences.en: He thought maybe he was even born in the wrong place.
sentences.zh: 他甚至觉得也许自己生错了地方。

sentences.en: I had to turn my feelings off to live normal.
sentences.zh: 我不得不关闭自己的情感才能正常生活。

sentences.en: He would often escape into his own world.
sentences.zh: 他经常逃进自己的世界里。

sentences.en: He loved music and designing things.
sentences.zh: 他热爱音乐和设计。

sentences.en: He once built his own handmade guitar.
sentences.zh: 他曾经自己亲手做过一把吉他。

sentences.en: I love creation.
sentences.zh: 我热爱创造。

sentences.en: Any kind.
sentences.zh: 任何种类的创造。

sentences.en: But C's doubts only grew harder and harder to ignore.
sentences.zh: 但C的疑虑变得越来越难以忽视。

sentences.en: My father.
sentences.zh: 我的父亲。

sentences.en: Like when he would ride in the car with his dad.
sentences.zh: 就像当他坐着他爸爸的车时。

sentences.en: He'd listen to Queen or the Bee Gees.
sentences.zh: 他会听皇后乐队或比吉斯的歌。

sentences.en: Bee Gees.
sentences.zh: 比吉斯乐队。

sentences.en: And we were watching American movies.
sentences.zh: 我们还在看美国电影。

sentences.en: And C himself would watch movies and shows about Westerners.
sentences.zh: 而且C自己也会看关于西方人的电影和节目。

sentences.en: We could see how they're similar to us.
sentences.zh: 我们可以看出他们和我们有多么相似。

sentences.en: So there wasn't a question that America is our enemy.
sentences.zh: 所以根本不存在美国是我们的敌人这种问题。

sentences.en: One of his favorite things to watch was an anime adaptation of Anne of Green Gables.
sentences.zh: 他最喜欢观看的东西之一是《绿山墙的安妮》的动画改编版。

sentences.en: She was an outsider, just like him.
sentences.zh: 她是一个局外人，就像他一样。

sentences.en: I just sympathize because my experience was similar to her.
sentences.zh: 我只是感同身受，因为我的经历和她很相似。

sentences.en: And he noticed other things.
sentences.zh: 而且他注意到了其他事情。

sentences.en: Like in the school scenes.
sentences.zh: 就像学校里的那些场景一样。

sentences.en: The boys and girls weren't separated.
sentences.zh: 男生和女生没有被分开。

sentences.en: They were together, sitting side by side, interacting with each other.
sentences.zh: 他们在一起，并排坐着，互相交流。

sentences.en: He wished his school was like that.
sentences.zh: 他希望自己的学校也是那样。

sentences.en: So much so that before going to sleep at night, he would imagine himself sitting in that classroom.
sentences.zh: 以至于每天晚上睡觉前，他都会想象自己坐在那个教室里。

sentences.en: As the years passed, C's thoughts shifted from doubts to disbelief.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，C的想法从怀疑变成了不信。

sentences.en: Disbelief in Islam.
sentences.zh: 对伊斯兰教的不信。

sentences.en: Disbelief in his government.
sentences.zh: 对他的政府的不信。

sentences.en: Disbelief in the Supreme Leader.
sentences.zh: 对最高领袖的不信。

sentences.en: Where, in his mind, all of this came from.
sentences.zh: 在他看来，这一切都源于此。

sentences.en: Everything they told us from the beginning was a big lie.
sentences.zh: 他们从一开始告诉我们的一切都是一个弥天大谎。

sentences.en: But he largely kept his feelings a secret.
sentences.zh: 但他基本上把自己的感受藏在心里。

sentences.en: Until holding them in became unbearable.
sentences.zh: 直到再也憋不住为止。

sentences.en: Suddenly, I have to do something to empty my mind from this.
sentences.zh: 突然间，我必须做点什么来清空脑子里的这些想法。

sentences.en: One night around midnight, when he was about 13 years old, he took a black spray paint bottle to a wall in his neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 一天午夜左右，大约在他13岁的时候，他拿着一瓶黑色喷漆来到了他社区的一面墙前。

sentences.en: And he spray painted a message.
